title: Hearty Garlicy Chinese Tofu Dumplings
description: Chewy, garlicky dumplings inspired by Yunnan cuisine, served steaming from a donabe with sesame oil and wok-hei for a festive ovo-vegetarian experience.
instructions: Press tofu with a clean towel to remove excess moisture then crumble it into a bowl.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, diced water chestnut, shredded cabbage, minced green onions, wok-hei, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, salt, and cornstarch to the tofu and mix until evenly coated.
Place a spoonful of filling onto each dumpling wrapper, leaving a small gap between pieces.
Moisten the edges of the wrapper with a little water and fold over to seal, pressing the edges to ensure no air pockets.
Heat a donabe over medium heat and add a splash of sesame oil to coat the bottom.
Spread the dumplings in a single layer, leaving space between them, and cook for 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden.
Add 1/4 cup water to the pot, cover immediately, and steam the dumplings for 5 minutes.
Remove the lid and let the water evaporate, then continue cooking for another 2 minutes to crisp the bottoms.
Transfer dumplings to a serving plate, drizzle with additional sesame oil, and sprinkle chopped green onions on top.
Serve hot with a side of steamed rice or enjoy solo for a festive dim-sum treat.
